title: Ghost rotationally invariant slave-boson approach to response functions
authors: Lee Tsung-Han, Melnick Corey, Lanatà Nicola, Kotliar Gabriel
abstract: We propose a finite-temperature Gaussian-fluctuation formalism for response functions within ghost rotationally invariant slave-boson (gRISB) theory and apply it to the two-dimensional Hubbard model. The gRISB magnetic phase boundary and static spin and charge susceptibilities capture the trends of dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), significantly improving upon standard RISB and the random phase approximation (RPA). At the RISB level, our formalism recovers the Kotliar-Ruckenstein response. The dynamical susceptibilities resolve paramagnons, low-energy sound modes, and high-energy Hubbard excitations. Because they are evaluated directly on the real-frequency axis, the results avoid Matsubara truncation, stochastic sampling, and numerical analytic continuation. We also introduce a conserving quasiparticle approximation that expresses the response in terms of dressed Green's functions and vertex corrections.
summary: This work develops and applies a ghost rotationally invariant slave-boson (gRISB) theory to study the two-dimensional Hubbard model. By using a Gaussian-fluctuation formalism, the authors calculate response functions directly on the real-frequency axis, significantly improving upon existing approximations. The results successfully capture key physical excitations and track the magnetic phase boundary in agreement with advanced methods like DMFT.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately computing response functions (spin and charge susceptibilities) in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly capturing the real-frequency spectral structure relevant to inelastic scattering experiments.
main_result: The proposed ghost rotationally invariant slave-boson (gRISB) formalism significantly improves upon standard approximations (RISB, RPA) by tracking the magnetic phase boundary and resolving key excitations like paramagnons and sound modes.
method: It employs a finite-temperature Gaussian-fluctuation formalism applied to the slave-boson theory, allowing direct calculation of susceptibilities on the real-frequency axis, thus bypassing problematic numerical continuation techniques.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the two-dimensional Hubbard model on a square lattice, described by the standard Hubbard Hamiltonian, and utilizes slave-boson decomposition techniques.
key_observables: Static and dynamical spin and charge susceptibilities ($\chi_{sp}, \chi_{ch}$), magnetic phase boundary, paramagnon excitations, and low-energy sound modes.
important_parameters: Hubbard interaction strength ($U$), electron filling ($n$), and temperature ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the validity of the gRISB theory and introduces a Conserving Quasiparticle Approximation (CQPA) to enforce physical constraints, though discrepancies with DMFT are noted due to finite auxiliary-bath truncation.
figures_summary: Figures compare the magnetic phase boundary across various theories (gRISB vs. DMFT); other figures show real-frequency spectra of spin and charge susceptibilities, comparing gRISB results against RISB and embedding formalisms.
paper_structure: The paper develops the gRISB formalism using Gaussian fluctuations, introduces the CQPA to enforce conservation laws, and validates the results by comparing static and dynamic susceptibilities against established methods like DMFT and field-derivative calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the rigorous development of a conserving approximation (CQPA) and the ability to calculate dynamics directly on the real-frequency axis are highly valuable theoretical tools applicable to open quantum systems and many-body dynamics simulations.
